subject: PrivOffer request - OrbitAI: commission ramp + NET90 and upfront credit
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@orbitai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private Offer request - OrbitAI: commission ramp + NET90 and upfront credit

Hi Elena,

Thanks for the productive demo yesterday — excited by the technical fit. Per our conversation, OrbitAI is requesting a private offer on the AWS marketplace with two non-standard items to close:

1) Payment terms: NET90 on invoices (they will be paying via centralized procurement).
2) Commercial: 35% rev-share year 1, stepping down to 25% year 2; OrbitAI is also asking for a $75k upfront credit against first-year consumption to cover onboarding.

I've attached the PrivOffer draft and an SOW for the pilot. If acceptable, I'll route this to Deal Desk for formal submission — but they specifically asked we escalate for exec approval on the NET90 and upfront credit.

Next step: ask for Exec OK on NET90 + upfront credit; commission ramp we can potentially model through a carve schedule.

Thanks,
Priyom
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: PrivOfferDraft-OrbitAI.docx (docx), SOW-OrbitAI-v1.pdf (pdf), commission-model.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Elena Rossi <elena@orbitai.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-09T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private Offer request - OrbitAI: commission ramp + NET90 and upfront credit

Priyom —

Confirmed. Procurement asked we put NET90 in writing; finance will issue a single purchase order for the first-year committed amount and then settle on NET90 terms thereafter. The $75k credit is critical to get our CFO comfortable with the pilot timing. Without the credit, we risk a delayed start (Q4).

I can confirm the commercial team is ok with the ramp (35% -> 25%) if year 1 is protected via a minimum ARR threshold we discussed ($250k). Happy to take the PrivOffer as a formal DocuSign once Redwood confirms internal approvals.

Best,
Elena
Head of Strategic Partnerships, OrbitAI
procurement@orbitai.com

Folks —

Looping Deal Desk and finance/partner ops. OrbitAI (strategic ISV) is asking for: NET90 + $75k upfront credit (applied against year-1 consumption), and a rev-share schedule 35% Y1 -> 25% Y2 with a $250k minimum ARR protection.

Attachments: PrivOfferDraft-OrbitAI.docx, commission-model.xlsx, SOW-OrbitAI-v1.pdf

Can we get an eval on:
- Legal/risk on NET90 for marketplace private offers (any procurement gating we've seen)
- Financial impact of the $75k credit + how it shows up against rev-share accounting
- Whether we can model the ramp in the private offer metadata (or if we need to handle via separate invoicing/credits)

Request: Executive approval required for NET90 and upfront credit; recommend Marissa or a delegated exec weigh in. Need decision by EOD Tuesday to keep Q4 pilot timeline.

Thanks,
Priyom

Priyom —

Thanks for the background. I agree OrbitAI is strategic and the pilot cadence matters. My position: approve the commission ramp as structured conditioned on the $250k minimum ARR protection. For the NET90 and $75k upfront credit, I need a mitigant from finance (Monica) that shows cashflow exposure and a simple clawback if they churn before 6 months of consumption.

Karthik — can you and finance propose a short clawback / offset mechanism (credit recoup over 3 invoices) and confirm how this impacts partner commission? If the proposal is reasonable, I can sign off on NET90 + the $75k credit.

Marissa Cole
VP, Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Marissa / team —

Attached a short model (commission-model.xlsx) and proposed clawback language: 100% recoup of the upfront credit if total billed consumption < $50k within first 90 days; otherwise, recoup pro rata across remaining invoices until credit is offset. Commission will be paid on net receipts; for clawback, we recommend withholding 100% of partner commission on the first two invoices after discovery of shortfall, then re-true-up on month 3.

Finance input — Monica, does that mechanism materially change our revenue recognition or collection exposure? If acceptable, I'll update PrivOfferDraft to include the clause and route for Marissa sign-off.

-Karthik

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-08-11T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private Offer request - OrbitAI: commission ramp + NET90 and upfront credit

Team —

Reviewed the proposed clawback. Key points:
- Cash exposure under NET90 is manageable for this cohort if we gate the pilot P.O. to the committed minimum ($250k) and require the purchase order to be issued up front.
- The clawback language as drafted (100% recoup if < $50k in 90 days, otherwise pro rata) is acceptable from a collections perspective; we recommend a 6-month lookback window for detecting material non-payment before escalating to collections.
- Revenue recognition: upfront credit will be handled as a contra-revenue item against the first invoice series; rev-share payouts will be reported on net receipts. No material accounting red flags but we will need to track the clawback reserve in the partner ledger.

Given the mitigants above, Marissa — you have my thumbs up to approve NET90 + $75k upfront credit, provided the PO is issued and the PrivOffer includes the clawback.

Monica Patel
Director, Finance Operations | Redwood Inference
